# Kassapa Saṁyutta (SN 16)

**ID:** SN 16
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kassapasaṁyutta* constitutes Chapter V of the *Nidānavagga* in the *Saṁyuttanikāya* [Bodhi 2003]. It consists of a cycle of discourses centered on the Venerable Mahākassapa, who was extolled by the Buddha as his foremost disciple in the observance of austere ascetic practices (*dhutaṅga*) [Bodhi 2003; Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. The collection portrays Mahākassapa's exemplary contentment with modest requisites, his deep meditative realizations (*jhāna* and direct knowledges), and his dedication to the longevity and discipline of the monastic community [Bodhi 2003; SuttaCentral]. Notable episodes recount his exchange of robes with the Buddha and attainment of arahantship seven days after his ordination (SN 16.11), the Buddha inviting him to instruct the assembly on equal footing ("Either I, Kassapa, should exhort the monks, or you", SN 16.6), and his inquiry regarding the future decline of the true Dhamma accompanied by a proliferation of monastic rules (SN 16.13) [Flores 2008; Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Sujato & Brahmali 2015].

Textual parallels between the Pali *Kassapasaṁyutta* and the two extant Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* translations—the complete Sarvāstivāda SĀ (T 99) and the "other" *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 100)—exhibit an unusually exact correspondence in both sequence and content, differing primarily by two extra discourses placed at the beginning of the Pali collection and the relative placement of the *Jiṇṇasutta* (SN 16.5) [Sujato 2012; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also identifies parallels in the *Ekottarikāgama* (EĀ 12.6 and 41.5) and a Sanskrit narrative parallel to SN 16.11 in the *Mahāvastu* [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text extensively with T 99, T 100, the *Mahāvastu-avadāna*, the individual Chinese *Yueyu jing* (T 121, aligning with SN 16.3), and various Mahāyāna and scholastic treatises including the *Śrāvakabhūmi* and *Arthaviniścayasūtra* [DharmaNexus]. In Pali literature, DharmaNexus detects significant formulaic reuse between this saṁyutta and numerous chapters of the *Aṅguttaranikāya* (particularly AN 10, AN 5, AN 3, and AN 4) as well as *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12) and *Abyākata Saṁyutta* (SN 44) [DharmaNexus].
